payload.name: Preserve-explicit-general-claims-in-event-memories
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from multiple messages, if the speaker explicitly mentions a general activity or category, include that claim as a distinct fact even when specific examples are also recorded.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes an experience across multiple turns, include every explicitly stated general activity or category in the memory content, even when you also list specific examples—the general claim is independently queryable.
Re-check all source messages for umbrella terms and quantifiers (e.g., 'many', 'various', 'lots of') and represent them in the candidate; do not collapse the umbrella into its examples.

solves: The extraction candidate summarized a trip by specific activities but omitted the explicit umbrella claim 'went on many excursions', leaving the memory incomplete for a later query about that general activity. The underlying mechanism is dropping a general, independently queryable claim once its examples are captured. This rule applies to any multi-turn event extraction where a speaker states both a category and instances; preserving the category prevents partial-coverage failures.
